title: Closed immersions among universally closed morphisms
statement: Let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Then $g$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] if and only if $g$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] and universally injective [def-weil-radicial-morphism].

source.place: Tag 04XV, etale-lemma-characterize-closed-immersion, equivalence (1) and (5), with universal closedness fixed as a hypothesis; diagonal argument from Tag 05VH, etale-lemma-universally-injective-unramified.

proof.text: Assume $g$ is a closed immersion. By [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed], it is proper and a monomorphism, hence locally of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $P=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $gp_1=gp_2$, cancellation gives $p_1=p_2$. Thus $p_1\Delta_g=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $\Delta_gp_1=\mathrm{id}_P$, the latter checked on both projections. Therefore $\Delta_g$ is an isomorphism, so identifies $X$ with the whole open subscheme $P$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. The definition [def-weil-unramified-morphism] gives unramifiedness. The diagonal is also surjective, so the equivalence in [def-weil-radicial-morphism] gives universal injectivity.

source.place: Tag 04XV, (1) implies (2); Tag 05VH, (3) implies (1) and monomorphism criterion, expanded using the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: Conversely assume $g$ is unramified and universally injective. By [def-weil-unramified-morphism], $g$ is locally of finite type and $\Delta_g:X\to P$ is an open immersion. By the diagonal-surjectivity equivalence of [def-weil-radicial-morphism], $\Delta_g$ is surjective. An open immersion identifies its source with the open subscheme on its image [def-weil-open-immersion]; here that image is all of $P$, so $\Delta_g$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05VH, proof of (2) implies (1): the diagonal is a surjective open immersion.

proof.text: For any scheme $T$ and $a,b:T\to X$ with $ga=gb$, form $(a,b):T\to P$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $\Delta_g$ is invertible, $(a,b)=\Delta_gc$ for $c=\Delta_g^{-1}(a,b)$. Its two projections give $a=c=b$. Thus $g$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05VH, proof of (2) implies (1), final assertion that an isomorphic diagonal gives a monomorphism.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-scheme-monomorphism-separated], $g$ is separated. Its assumed universal closedness gives quasi-compactness by [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-quasi-compact]. Together with local finite type from step 2 this gives finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $g$ is proper by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply the reverse implication of [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] to this proper monomorphism to obtain a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 04XV, (6) implies (1), assembled through its equivalent proper-monomorphism criterion (2); Tag 04XU supplies quasi-compactness.

proof_origin.place: Tags 04XV (lemma-characterize-closed-immersion) and 05VH (lemma-universally-injective-unramified), expanded through Tag 04XU and the existing proper-monomorphism criterion.
